mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Korean corporate registration extract or certificate of registered matters)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain the certified registration extract from the Korean court registry; have the true copy notarized by a Korean notary public if required by the receiving authority; then obtain a single Hague Apostille from the Consular/Apostille Division of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. If the destination jurisdiction is not a Hague Apostille Convention state, do not attach the apostille; instead present the notarized document directly to the destination country's embassy or consulate for consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (tax clearance certificate / certificate of corporate tax payment and non-arrars)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea, relevant regional tax office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Request the tax clearance certificate from the National Tax Service; have the signature or office seal notarized by a Korean notary public; then affix a single Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for use in a Hague destination. For a non-Hague destination, the document must be taken through consular legalization at the destination country's embassy or consulate only. Never apply both apostille and consular legalization to the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney for opening bank account and signing agreements
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Chusik Hoesa, countersigned by the director and corporate secretary, with Korean notarization
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Prepare a bilingual Board Resolution and Power of Attorney; execute it under the company seal; arrange Korean notarization of the signatures and seal registration; then obtain one Hague Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for Hague destinations. Where consular legalization applies because the destination is outside the Apostille Convention, use only the consular legalization route of the destination state without any apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Court Registration Office where the incorporation is registered
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Take a certified copy of the registered Articles of Association issued by the court registry; have it certified by a Korean notary public; then obtain a single Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea. For non-Hague destination states, the same certified document must be legalized exclusively by the destination state's embassy or consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a Korean commercial bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The Korean bank selected for the company's operating account, signed by the branch manager and compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank must issue the reference letter on bank letterhead with original branch manager signature and bank seal; the bank's signal authority is notarized by a Korean notary public; then the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea appends a single Hague Apostille for a Hague destination. If the destination country is not a member of the Apostille Convention, submit the notarized bank letter to that country's embassy or consulate in Korea for consular legalization instead. Apostille and consular legalization must not be layered on the same document.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every shareholder, director, UBO, signatory and agent must be screened before appointment using a risk-based approach against KOFIU watchlists, Korean financial institution alerts, OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions listings, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU consolidated list, UK HMT sanctions list, and publicly available adverse media and PEP databases. PEP screening includes domestic and foreign PEPs and international organization senior officials. Screening must be refreshed continuously, especially before each Apple IAP or Google Play settlement cycle, and any hit requires enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, a documented risk decision, and a Suspicious Transaction Report to KOFIU where required. The commercial model being low-risk does not permit waiver of any screening requirement.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (IRO) of the Supreme Court of Korea at https://www.iros.go.kr; supplemental business and VAT-name verification through National Tax Service HomeTax at https://www.hometax.go.kr.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory registered name of a Chusik Hoesa must be in Korean Hangul; Latin-script words may be used as trading names but not as the primary registered-name token. Chinese characters (Hanja) and Chinese-character-only names are not accepted as statutory names. The four-tier naming convention requires: (i) a distinctive proprietary or coined element identifying the webtoon/comic publishing business; (ii) a business descriptor or industry term; (iii) the exact corporate suffix 'Chusik' or 'Chusik Hoesa' (stock corporation); and (iv) an optional English transliteration that is phonetically equivalent to the Hangul name. Phonetic transliteration into Hangul is mandatory; clearance is refused if the proposed Hangul name is identical or phonetically confusingly similar to another registered company in the same business line.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: When the registry officer issues a written refusal order citing confusing similarity or a prohibited token, the applicant has 14 calendar days from receipt to file a written objection with the same registration court, attaching a corrected proposed name, a comparison table of conflicting names, and a legal memorandum demonstrating the absence of phonetic or visual identity in the same business category. If the registry upholds the refusal, the applicant may file an immediate appeal with the competent district court under the Korean Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure within 14 days of the refusal notice. A further appeal to the Supreme Court on a question of law is available only sparingly; the most commercially efficient remedy is to file a new name preclearance application with a fresh distinctive token.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Under the Commercial Act and court registration practice, a post-office box or mail-forwarding service is not a valid registered office. A virtual office may be conditionally tolerated by regional tax offices for administrative service and VAT-invoice mailing, but it is not accepted as the statutory registered seat by Korean courts. For an ISIC 9000 / NAICS 511130 digital webtoon publishing company receiving Apple IAP and Google Play Billing proceeds, Korean banks will ordinarily reject a virtual-office-only arrangement for corporate account opening because CDD requires a physical business address, lease proof, utility receipts and management access. A serviced co-working space with a private assigned room and physical signage can satisfy the registry and bank requirements only if the service provider allows government and bank inspections, board meetings and mail receipt at that address. Pure mailbox programs are not permissible.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspections: (1) physical signage at the registered address; (2) corporate name plate; (3) lease agreement in the company's name; (4) utility bill under company name; (5) staff or responsible officer present during working hours; (6) accessible accounting records and VAT invoices; (7) board-meeting minutes and registers; (8) service contracts evidencing webtoon publishing operations; (9) device or server infrastructure supporting the digital content business. Quantified risk: a low-margin digital publisher with a real leased office and accurate filings faces roughly 10% annualized probability of an unannounced municipal tax or registry inspection. Risk increases to 25% to 40% if the company uses a virtual address only, has inconsistent IAP settlement reporting, or applies VAT zero-rating on foreign webtoon syndication proceeds without documentation. Each missing checklist item increases inspection likelihood by 5 to 10 percentage points.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Sections 288 through 314 (incorporation, articles of incorporation, capital), Section 329 (paid-in capital), Section 340 (issuance of shares), Section 363 (first board of directors meeting), and Section 5 of the Corporate Registration Act; also subject to the Framework Act on Foreign Investment for foreign shareholders.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Court Registry Office, Registration Division of the Seoul Central District Court, Republic of Korea (also accepts applications through the Supreme Court e-Registry online portal at www.iros.go.kr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Corporate Registration (Corporate Registration Certificate, 법인등기부) issued by the competent court registry; the incorporation is finalized upon registration of the articles of incorporation and appointment of directors and auditors in the commercial registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Korean Commercial Act does not impose a statutory minimum paid-in capital for a Chusik Hoesa. However, funds must be held in a corporate banking account and must be sufficient to cover initial operating expenses. No escrow or blocked account is required for incorporation; capital verification is completed via a capital deposit certificate issued by the financial institution where the paid-in capital is deposited.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] (CHUSIK HOESA), A COMPANY INCORPORATED UNDER THE LAWS OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA

WHEREAS the incorporators of the Company have duly executed and subscribed to the Articles of Incorporation in accordance with the Korean Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended);

WHEREAS the paid-in capital stated in the Articles of Incorporation has been fully paid into the corporate bank account of the Company, and a capital deposit certificate has been issued by the receiving financial institution;

WHEREAS the incorporators have convened this first meeting of the Board of Directors to effect the formal organization of the Company and to authorize the establishment of its corporate and banking infrastructure;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED unanimously by the Board, in accordance with Article 363 of the Korean Commercial Act, that:

1. RESOLVED that the payment of the subscribed capital set forth in the Articles of Incorporation, being KRW __________ (equivalent to not less than the amount necessary for the Company's initial operations), is hereby ratified and accepted, and the capital deposit certificate shall be preserved in the corporate minute book.

2. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be, and is hereby, fixed and confirmed at [insert full registered address], Republic of Korea, and the Chief Executive Officer is authorized to file the necessary registration with the Seoul Central District Court Registry Office and to execute any lease or service agreement in respect of such office.

3. RESOLVED that the following persons are hereby appointed as statutory officers for the first term of office in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation: (a) [Name], as Chief Executive Officer (대표이사), with full authority to bind the Company; (b) [Name], as Chief Financial Officer (재무이사), with authority to open, operate, and close bank accounts; and (c) [Name], as Auditor (감사), if required by the Articles. Each officer shall hold office for a term not exceeding the statutory maximum under the Commercial Act.

4. RESOLVED that the Chief Executive Officer is expressly authorized, with the concurrence of the Chief Financial Officer, to open and maintain corporate deposit and operating accounts with a commercial bank of repute in the Republic of Korea, to designate authorized signatories, and to execute such account opening agreements, internet banking mandates, and payment service authorizations as may be necessary, including but not limited to Apple IAP and Google Play Billing settlement accounts.

5. RESOLVED that this Resolution shall be effective immediately, that the Company Secretary is directed to file a certified copy of this Resolution with the registry authorities as required, and that all officers, directors, and agents of the Company are hereby authorized and instructed to carry out the foregoing resolutions and to perform all acts and execute all documents necessary to fulfill the business purpose of the Company as set forth in the Articles of Incorporation, namely digital webtoon publishing, multilingual chapter unlocking, and related content syndication and distribution.

6. RESOLVED FURTHER that any officer of the Company may, from time to time, certify as to the adoption of this Resolution and the authority of the persons designated herein for the purpose of dealing with regulatory, banking, or commercial counterparties.

ADOPTED this ___ day of _________, 20___, by unanimous written consent of all incumbent directors. This Resolution is signed by the Chairman of the Board, attested by the Company Secretary, and entered in the corporate register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize Articles of Incorporation and Internal Governance Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Korean Notary Public (인증변호사 or 공증인) and the appointed Incorporating Attorney; the articles are later filed with the Seoul Central District Court Registry Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Korean attorney to draft the Articles of Incorporation, the Minutes of the Incorporators' Meeting, and the First Board Resolution text. The Articles must include the company name, business purpose (digital webtoon publishing and multilingual content syndication), total authorized shares, initial paid-in capital amount, registered office address, and the names of incorporators. The draft must be certified by a Korean notary public or, in the alternative, by a certified Korean attorney who prepared the documentation. The incorporating attorney will then obtain the consent of all incorporators, verify their identity and capacity, and arrange for the executory signature on each page. The final notarized Articles must bear the exact corporate name in Korean (e.g., 주식회사 __________) and must clearly limit the company's business scope to lawful digital content activities. The attorney will prepare an ancillary legal opinion confirming that the Articles do not violate the Korean Commercial Act and that no governmental pre-approval is required for webtoon publishing. This step is completed when the notarized Articles and certified resolutions are ready for court filing.
required_dossiers: Completed and notarized Articles of Incorporation (정관) in Korean with English translation
Consent forms and passport copies of all incorporators and initial directors
Attorney's legal opinion on compliance with the Commercial Act
Power of attorney for incorporation (위임장) executed by each incorporator
Notice of appointment of representative director (대표이사)
Capital deposit certificate or bank statement proving deposit of paid-in capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the attorney queries any provision of the Articles, the incorporators must file a written addendum or a revised Articles page and re-notarize the affected clauses. If the draft contains ambiguous business purposes, the attorney will issue a supplementary opinion and resubmit. Where identities are insufficiently documented, the incorporators shall provide apostilled identity documents within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Application with the Seoul Central District Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Seoul Central District Court Registry Office (법원등기국) through the Supreme Court Electronic Registration Portal (iros.go.kr) or in-person filing at the Registry counter at 25 Pyongchang-ro, Jongno-gu, Seoul.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the First Board Resolution, and all supporting dossiers to the competent registry authority. The application must include Form 2 (Company Registration Application), Form 8 (Notice of Appointment of Directors), and Form 10 (Declaration of Paid-in Capital). The registry officer will verify that the Articles comply with the Commercial Act, that the capital deposit certificate is authentic, that all directors have accepted their appointments, and that no disqualifying criminal or disqualification history applies to the directors. The officer will then assign a corporate registration number (법인번호) and enter the company into the Commercial Registry. For foreign shareholders, the application must be accompanied by an apostilled certificate of corporate existence and power of attorney; if the shareholder is an individual, a passport copy with notarization and apostille is required. After the registry examination, the issuance of the Certificate of Corporate Registration may be requested immediately, usually on the same day. The certificate must be collected personally by an attorney or through registered mail.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (original)
First Board Resolution (certified copy)
Capital deposit certificate (issued by bank)
Application forms prescribed by the court registration rules (certified copies)
Power of attorney for the attorney filing the application
Report on payment of registration tax and education tax (receipt)
Identification documents of directors and auditor, with apostille for non-Korean residents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a refusal or deficiency notice, the attorney must cure the missing item within 5 business days. Common deficiencies include missing stamp duty, defective capital deposit certificate, or inaccurate address. The attorney may request a formal supplemental notice and file a corrected application. If the refusal is based on a legal defect in the Articles, the incorporators must convene a general shareholders meeting to amend the Articles and then recommence filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Corporate Bank Account and Deposit Paid-in Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A major commercial bank in the Republic of Korea (e.g., Shinhan Bank, Kookmin Bank, Woori Bank, or Hana Bank) at a branch designated by the Company; for foreign majority shareholders, a branch with international corporate banking capability.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before filing the incorporation application (or immediately after the registry filing), the designated Chief Financial Officer and the Chief Executive Officer must personally visit the bank with the corporate registration certificate and the original Articles of Incorporation. The bank will verify the identity of the directors and beneficial owners, conduct customer due diligence in accordance with the Financial Transactions Reports Act, and open a corporate current account and a deposit account. The paid-in capital amount stated in the Articles must be transferred from the incorporators' personal accounts to the corporate account, and the bank will issue a capital deposit certificate (금융기관 거래확인서). This certificate is a mandatory attachment to the incorporation filing, and it proves the actual payment of the subscribed capital. The bank will also set up internet banking credentials and, if the company intends to receive payments from Apple IAP or Google Play Billing, an escrow settlement account or separate publisher settlement account may be opened. All banking mandates and signatory powers must be aligned with the First Board Resolution.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Corporate Registration (if already issued) or number of the pending application
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Corporate seal certificate (인감증명서) issued by the registry
Passports and personal resident registrations of directors
Board resolution authorizing the opening of bank accounts
Business plan or initial contract evidencing intended webtoon publishing operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank suspends the account opening due to incomplete beneficial ownership disclosure, the company must provide a written explanation of the corporate chain and extended shareholder registry. For non-Korean directors, the bank may require additional apostilled passports or a local Alien Registration Card. The company may choose a different bank branch or bank if the initial request is denied for over 7 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Corporate Tax Accounts, Social Insurance, and Value-Added Tax Profile
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office (세무서) under the National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea, and the local National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, and Korea Workers' Compensation & Welfare Service (for any future employees).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days from the date of incorporation registration, the company must file a Business Registration Application (사업자등록신청서) with the relevant District Tax Office (usually the one having jurisdiction over the registered office). The application must be accompanied by the Certificate of Corporate Registration, the Articles of Incorporation, and a power of attorney for the tax accountant. The tax office will issue a Business Registration Certificate with a tax identification number (사업자등록번호) and a TIN for corporate tax purposes. The company must also register for Value-Added Tax and, if it will employ staff, register as a workplace for four major social insurance programs (national pension, health insurance, employment insurance, industrial accident insurance). For digital content syndication, the National Tax Service may require an obligation to withhold and remit royalty income tax on payments to other content creators or foreign platform operators. The company must also register for electronic tax invoice issuance through the National Tax Service's e-invoice system (홈택스).
required_dossiers: Certificate of Corporate Registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Business Registration Application form (form prescribed by the National Tax Service)
Certificate of corporate seal and personal seal certificates of directors
Lease agreement or proof of office location
Authority for the tax agent (전자수임장) if filed electronically
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the business purpose or the physical location of the registered office, the company must provide a lease agreement or a virtual office service agreement. If the business purpose is deemed to require a specific tax classification, the tax office may request a supplementary explanation; the tax accountant must respond within 5 business days. If the registration is delayed, the company can continue operating but may be subject to a late registration surcharge; the remedy is to file as soon as possible and apply for penalty reduction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Contents Industry Optional Clearances and Webtoon Syndication Compliance Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Media Rating Board (KMRB) for voluntary content rating of webtoons, the Korea Communications Standards Commission (KCSC) for online content regulation, and the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism (MCST) for digital content dissemination; also the Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC) for relevant privacy clearances.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Although the subject business is purely digital and does not require a physical operating license, a digital webtoon publisher with multilingual chapter unlocking must comply with the Act on the Promotion of Information and Communications Network Utilization and Data Protection, as well as the Content Industry Promotion Act. The company must verify whether any webtoon content that includes adult or violent themes requires a mandatory rating from the Korea Media Rating Board or a submission to the KCSC. For monetization via Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, the company must register as a content provider with each platform and comply with their content policy. From a privacy perspective, the company must set up a privacy policy and register any information processing device (IT system) with the PIPC if personal data is processed on a large scale. The MCST may require a 'Digital Contents Distribution Business' self-declaration, but no government permit is needed. The company should obtain a written legal opinion confirming that no manufacturing, handling, or warehousing license is applicable. This step may be completed concurrently with Step 4 but must be finalized before the first commercial release.
required_dossiers: Business Registration Certificate
Memorandum describing the webtoon content types and target jurisdictions
Apple/Google developer account registration confirmation
Privacy policy and data processing inventory for PIPC compliance
Voluntary rating submission form to KMRB (if content is moderate or higher)
Legal opinion on ISIC 9000 classification and exemption from industrial licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the KCSC or KMRB flags certain content as needing rating, the company must file the content for evaluation and wait for the rating decision; while the rating is pending, the content cannot be released. If the PIPC identifies privacy gaps, the company must revise its privacy policy and submit an internal correction plan. For platform policy issues, the company must align its app metadata and disclosure with Apple and Google requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the business is classified under ISIC 9000 (Creative, arts and entertainment activities) for webtoon publishing and syndication; it does not involve physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing. No industrial licensing board or municipal agency is competent for this pure digital content activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no operating license is required for digital webtoon publication. The company only needs the Business Registration Certificate issued by the District Tax Office and, where applicable, an optional content rating from the Korea Media Rating Board for restricted content.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - no environmental permitting authority supervises this digital activity; the Ministry of Environment's regulations apply only to physical installations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the company has no physical plant, no wastewater discharge, no VOC emissions, no hazardous waste streams, and no construction. An Environmental Impact Assessment authorization is not required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no quantitative thresholds apply. The company's sole operational footprint is the processing of digital content on servers, which is governed by the Personal Information Protection Act and the Act on the Promotion of Information and Communications Network Utilization, not by environmental law.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - the company is an e-publisher with no physical production site, no storage of flammable materials, no heavy machinery, and no workforce above the small-scale threshold that would trigger a special fire safety inspection. The registered office, being a standard commercial lease, must retain a valid 'Fire and Evacuation Plan' (that plan is obtained by the property owner from the local fire station) and shall comply with ordinary building management rules. No separate Civil Defense fire permit is required for a pure digital content operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea, with the HomeTax electronic tax portal (www.hometax.go.kr) for registration, filing, and e-Tax Invoice reporting; export declarations are processed by the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS trade portal (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity cannot directly register as the domestic taxpayer; it must first incorporate or acquire a Chusik Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act and complete court registration at the local District Court registry. Immediately after incorporation, the Chusik Hoesa must apply for a Business Registration Certificate with the competent NTS District Tax Office through HomeTax using the representative's digital certificate and an authorized foreign power of attorney where directors are outside Korea. Required documentation includes the corporate registration certificate, articles of incorporation, proof of the registered address, lease or ownership documents for the domestic place of business, the statutory seat designation, identification of shareholders and directors, and evidence of the foreign capital contribution under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act where applicable. The tax office will issue the 10-digit corporate registration number, which functions as the Tax Identification Number and is mandatory for issuing e-Tax Invoices. The application must be finalized before the company enters its first VAT-taxable supply chain, and the registration will be updated for any domestic branch, place of business, or warehouse separately if a permanent establishment is later added.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None - Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch entity election. A Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily treated as a domestic corporation subject to entity-level corporate income tax on worldwide income, regardless of non-resident shareholder composition.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT), governed by the Value-Added Tax Act and enforced by the National Tax Service.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold applies to a Chusik Hoesa; every corporate VAT taxpayer must register at the commencement of business activities. The KRW 80 million simplified-taxpayer threshold applies only to certain individual entrepreneurs and is not available to corporations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The Chusik Hoesa must issue e-Tax Invoices electronically through NTS HomeTax, EDI, or NTS-approved API integration, and must transmit tax-invoice data to the NTS electronic clearing database without using physical fiscal stamps. E-invoice details must be submitted to the NTS database by the day after issuance. B2C transactions from webtoon distribution made through Apple IAP or Google Play Billing must be substantiated by the platform settlement reports, e-payment transaction records, and cash-receipt system entries where required. The NTS carries out near-real-time matching of e-Tax Invoices, app-store payment data, and cash receipts for anti-fraud clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Article 24 of the Value-Added Tax Act for exported goods and for services supplied to or used outside Korea, including qualifying offshore digital content syndication. For webtoon chapter-unlocking services, the Chusik Hoesa must prove that the service is supplied to a non-resident purchaser or foreign platform, the digital content is delivered or consumed outside the Korean customs territory, and the consideration is remitted through a Korean foreign exchange bank or another traceable foreign-sourced payment channel. The service export must satisfy the Enforcement Decree test for export services, and the zero-rated supply is recognized only where the place of supply is outside Korea and the contracting counterparty is not a Korean domestic consumer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Electronic Export Declaration (customs clearance confirmation issued through UNI-PASS)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing shipment to a foreign consignee, where physical goods are involved
Commercial Invoice and the executed digital content license or webtoon syndication agreement
Foreign Exchange Bank Export Proceeds Receipt Confirmation issued by a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank as evidence of collection of foreign currency
Zero-rated e-Tax Invoice issued through NTS HomeTax for the exported digital service
Platform settlement statements from Apple IAP or Google Play Billing showing foreign-origin payments and deduction of app-store commissions
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service may reject zero-rating where any part of the documentation bundle is missing, inconsistent, or untimely. Rejected export supplies are recharacterized as taxable domestic supplies, resulting in assessment of 10% VAT on the full consideration, recovery of any previously claimed input VAT credits, understatement surcharges of up to 40% for fraudulent filings plus daily late-payment interest, and potential civil penalties. Fraudulent zero-rating claims may also be referred for criminal investigation under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, and the NTS closely audits webtoon syndication platforms by cross-referencing app-store payment data, foreign-exchange remittance records, and Korean consumer access logs to detect fictionally exported digital content.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (the Central Bank of the Republic of Korea), together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Korea Customs Service in the administration of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South Korean won (KRW) is a floating, generally freely convertible currency for current account transactions such as export proceeds, service fees, royalties, and digital content syndication payments. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act separates current account from capital account treatment. Current account transactions are liberalized and can be settled through designated foreign exchange banks using identity-based reporting. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment, equity subscription, cross-border loans, and issuance of shares to non-residents, are also broadly liberalized but require mandatory pre-reporting or post-reporting to the Bank of Korea through a designated foreign exchange bank. There are no surrender requirements restricting the holding of export proceeds; exporters may maintain foreign currency in local accounts and convert at market rates. Profit remittance is achievable via lawful dividend distribution, but the treasurer must first satisfy corporate income tax settlement, verify distributable retained earnings under Korean Commercial Act rules, and pay the applicable dividend withholding tax for residents or the treaty-reduced rate for non-residents. In a crisis scenario, the Minister of Economy and Finance may impose temporary FX transaction restrictions with IMF notification, but such measures are exceptional and not part of the ordinary treasury process.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, export proceeds must be collected within one year from the date of export declaration. An extension of up to six months may be granted by the Korean authorities through the designated foreign exchange bank where justifiable commercial grounds are proved. No statutory percentage of export proceeds must be surrendered or converted into Korean won; the former foreign exchange concentration and surrender system has been abolished. Exporters may keep the full amount in a domestic foreign currency deposit account, disburse it for permitted purposes, or convert it into KRW at a market rate. In all cases, the designated bank should record the collection, and any receipt or payment exceeding the regulatory reporting threshold must be filed under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for FDI proceeds and Basic Operational Currency Account for daily KRW settlement
Capital Escrow Account for FDI proceeds and Basic Operational Currency Account for daily KRW settlement
Capital Escrow Account for FDI proceeds and Basic Operational Currency Account for daily KRW settlement

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility as a primary treasury rail. Offshore digital EMI providers such as Revolut, Payoneer, and Wise are not licensed as banks under the Korean Banking Act and are not designated foreign exchange banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. They therefore cannot open a domestic KRW settlement account for a Korean Chusik Hoesa, cannot perform statutory foreign exchange reporting, and cannot accept the capital-injection or dividend-remittance reporting functions that Korean residency requires. Such EMIs may be used only as auxiliary collection wallets for non-Korean platform sales, with balances swept through SWIFT MT103 wires into a designated foreign exchange bank in Korea. For all regulatory purposes, the Korean entity must maintain its operating capital and FX reporting relationships with a domestic Tier-1 bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean domestic entities with resident Korean directors and beneficial owners may complete account opening through a non-face-to-face process using accredited video identification, a Korean digital certificate, and ARS phone authentication. Non-resident foreign directors or controlling shareholders are generally required to appear in person at the corporate banking branch, or to execute a notarized power of attorney with apostille and consular legalization authorizing a named Korean agent to attend the branch and complete the interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not universally recognized; Korean Tier-1 banks will usually require the non-resident individual to appear at an overseas branch of the bank or at a Korean embassy or consulate to verify identity and sign the required documentation. For the statutory directors of the Chusik Hoesa, the bank will insist on either in-branch physical appearance of the authorized board members or a clear, sequentially complete documentary chain of proxy authority supported by video identity verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained dilution or layered ownership of the Chusik Hoesa with non-resident shareholders in offshore digital content licensing vehicles.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original or certified copy of the shareholder registry, corporate seal certificate, statutory books, notarized UBO declaration for every ten percent shareholder, ownership organogram, certificate of incorporation of each offshore vehicle, source-of-wealth statements, bank reference letters from the remitting bank, and audited financial statements for the last two years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared low-risk webtoon publishing activity and expected heavy cross-border outbound payments to freelance artists, translation studios, and syndication agents in multiple jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed artist and studio service agreements, translation and sub-licensing contracts, royalty schedules, monthly IP portfolio reports, tax invoices and withholding certificates, payment processor payout statements from Apple and Google, and an audit trail linking each disbursement to a specific chapter title or licensed territory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, adverse media, or politically exposed person hits on counterparties, beneficial owners, or the webtoon platform aggregator.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: World-Check or LexisNexis Diligence screening reports for all named parties, official identity documents, passport copies, PEP declarations, sanctions jurisdiction analysis, written reasonableness explanations, and independent legal counsel opinion confirming the absence of restricted-party exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a non-resident investor without clear Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and Foreign Investment Promotion Act reporting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign Investment Report or stock acquisition report accepted by the designated foreign exchange bank, bank certificate of foreign currency deposit, inbound SWIFT MT103 transaction confirmation, share subscription agreement, paid-in capital certificate, confirmation of corporate registration amendment, and an undertaking to file all post-transaction reports through the bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All non-resident equity injections must be routed to the Chusik Hoesa foreign currency deposit account at a designated foreign exchange bank in Korea. The remitter submits a SWIFT MT103 with full remitter and beneficiary name, address, and beneficiary account number, and clearly indicates the remittance purpose as FDI equity subscription in field 70 using the bank-assigned foreign exchange purpose code for direct investment in a domestic corporation. Under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, the investor files an investment report with KOTRA or the designated bank before or within twenty days after the remittance; the bank issues a foreign currency deposit certificate and capital verification confirms the paid-in share capital. The entity then files the share issuance report with the corporate registry and reflects the investment in its balance sheet. For amounts above the regulatory reporting threshold, the bank will separately submit the receipt report under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For digital webtoon syndication, outbound disbursements are primarily royalties and service fees, best executed by SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer with total plus charges, referencing the underlying contract and tax invoice. Korean banks settle these service payments through the Foreign Exchange Information Network and will file a payment report when the transaction exceeds the regulatory threshold or when the designated bank requires reporting. For print merchandise or physical publication, the entity may also use a commercial letter of credit as a sight or usance documentary credit in favor of offshore printers, and a documentary collection with documents against payment or documents against acceptance for lower-risk physical trade. However, documentary trade instruments are not necessary for pure digital chapter unlocking; the principal clearing rail for the webtoon business is the bank-to-bank MT103 network supported by service agreements, invoices, and withholding tax certificates.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla KRW/USD or KRW/JPY forward purchase and sale contracts permitted only to hedge current trade exposures such as Apple and Google payout receipts and royalty payment commitments, with underlying verification and no speculative open positions.

Non-deliverable forwards on KRW are available to non-resident financial institutions and certain permitted resident corporates with verified underlying exposure; for the Chusik Hoesa, an onshore forward is preferable and NDF access will require real-demand substantiation and designated bank approval.

Cross-currency swaps and FX options may be used only for hedging capital account exposures such as foreign currency debt, equity, dividends, and large royalty flows, and require the counterparty to be a domestic designated foreign exchange bank or a licensed international bank branch with full documentation of the underlying exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Shareholders and Approval of Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' internal corporate governance; minutes retained at registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months of the preceding fiscal year-end; customary practice is within 6 months of fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government filing penalty, but failure to hold the AGM may constitute a director breach and can be challenged by shareholders; persistent non-compliance may be cited in administrative or court actions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Financial Statements Submission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Corporate income tax return filed by March 31 for December fiscal year-end; fiscal year-end month-end plus 3 months
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Income tax surcharge of 20 percent of the understated amount for underreporting and 40 percent for failure to file; non-payment penalties of 0.66 percent per day; criminal sanctions possible for willful non-reporting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax Surtax Return (Corporate Income Tax Surtax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government / Metropolitan Office of Education via the local tax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Together with corporate income tax return; by March 31 following the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local income tax surcharge of 20 to 40 percent; additional arrears interest applies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Periodic Filing and Annual Settlement (if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Semiannual VAT filings: first period by April 25, second period by October 25; each filing covers a six-month return period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharge of 10 percent for failure to file a VAT return; additional 0.66 percent per day for unpaid tax

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Withholding and Social Insurance Annual Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service and National Pension Service / National Health Insurance Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Labor income withholding annual reconciliation by March 10 of the following year; social insurance contributions settled monthly
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late withholding surcharges up to 20 percent; social insurance arrears subject to collection enforcement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report Filing (when statutory audit threshold is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via the external audit management system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days from the fiscal year-end; audited financial statements must be tabled at the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or file audit report may trigger administrative fines up to KRW 20 million (approximately USD 15,000); registration or licensing impact for the entity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registry of Beneficial Ownership maintained by the relevant registry authority / National Tax Service under FATF-aligned rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days of the date of the annual general meeting; or as designated by the director of the competent registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to KRW 20 million for failure to report; criminal penalty possible for false or omitted beneficial ownership reporting

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory external audit required if any of the following is met: (a) total assets at fiscal year-end exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9 million); (b) total revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion (approximately USD 75 million); (c) number of employees is 300 or more and revenue and assets both exceed KRW 10 billion; (d) the company is a listed company or a financial institution; small corporations with total assets under KRW 5 billion may be eligible for exemption or simplified audit under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for mandatory audit entities; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) permitted for non-listed entities under the small business scope

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must promptly record any shareholding transfer in the Register of Members; an annual confirmation of ultimate beneficial ownership must be submitted to the competent registry authority within 30 days of the AGM or within any date directed by the registry, including details of each individual who directly or indirectly controls the company through shareholding, voting rights, or other means; share transfers are only opposable to the company upon registration in the Register of Members
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Board of Directors' Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 to USD 800 per annum for registered office and compliance agent services in Seoul local market
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 to USD 20,000 for a certified independent audit engagement depending on transaction volume, revenue size, and webtoon digital royalty documentation complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 2 billion; 21% from KRW 2 billion to KRW 30 billion; 24% in excess of KRW 30 billion
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A statutory income tax holiday is generally unavailable for ordinary domestic webtoon syndication corporations. Preferential relief may arise through the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and Free Economic Zone incentives for qualifying high-tech digital content operators, including a 50% to 100% corporate income tax holiday for the first 5 to 10 years in designated zones. Additional deductions and tax credits apply to research and development expenditure, job creation investment, and qualifying small and medium enterprises, reducing the effective rate below the statutory headline rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Tax Base and Tax Computation Statement) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the close of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year corporation, the filing and payment deadline is the last day of March of the following year. The deadline is extended to the next business day if the final day falls on a weekend or public holiday. Interim corporate tax prepayment is due within 2 months after the first half of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification: company name, tax identification number, registered corporate number, fiscal year-end date, paid-in capital, principal business code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned Korean Chusik Hoesa must use its Korean tax number and present accurate ultimate beneficial owner details for foreign shareholders. Non-resident parent company contact information must be captured in the supplementary schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue: total consideration from webtoon digital chapter sales, chapter unlocking revenue through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, IP licensing, advertising income, and syndication royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only revenue recognized in the Korean entity; export revenue and platform commissions must be shown gross with separate deductions for platform fees. Revenue deemed attributable to a foreign permanent establishment must be removed under the relevant tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: payroll for artists and editors, translation and localization costs, digital infrastructure and server expenses, platform commissions, marketing, rent, legal fees, and depreciation of intangible assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be supported by proper evidence and be incurred beneficially for the Korean entity. Costs charged from a foreign related party are deductible only if they satisfy the arm's length standard and adequate transfer pricing documentation is retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base calculation: net book income adjusted for nondeductible expenses, nontaxable income, special credits, and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Taxable income for a domestic Korean corporation includes worldwide income. Non-resident shareholders are not taxed on this return; the return computes the Korean entity's own corporate tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computation at the statutory progressive rates, plus the 10% local corporate income surtax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign parent must ensure no treaty rate relief is applied to the Korean entity's own income; this box is for computing the domestic tax liability only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing adjustments: amounts disallowed or added because of non-arm's-length cross-border transactions, including royalty payments to related IP companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign related-party transactions above the statutory documentation thresholds require attached Local File and Master File filings. The tax authority may adjust taxable income if the Korean licensee cannot demonstrate beneficial ownership of the licensed webtoon IP.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits for taxes paid abroad on Korean-source or foreign-source income, where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean corporation receives income from a foreign jurisdiction and suffered foreign withholding or corporate tax, the foreign tax credit is claimed here with a foreign tax credit calculation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable: total corporate income tax and local surtax after interim prepayments, withholding credits, and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any underpaid balance is due with the return. Non-resident shareholders must independently settle Korean dividend withholding upon distribution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a negligence penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax if filed within the following 5 days, escalating to 30% to 40% for later filings or intentional underreporting. Underreported tax is penalized at up to 40% if fraud is involved. Late payment attracts a daily interest surcharge of approximately 0.022% on the unpaid amount. Criminal liability may arise under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act for repeated or fraudulent nonfiling, with imprisonment up to 3 years and fines up to twice the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% for dividends paid by a Korean resident corporation to a non-resident corporate or individual shareholder, composed of a 20% national withholding tax and a 2% local income tax surcharge.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke an income tax treaty benefit, the non-resident shareholder must submit to the Korean withholding agent or the National Tax Service the Application for Reduction or Exemption of Non-Resident Withholding Tax, accompanied by a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the shareholder's residence jurisdiction, a beneficial ownership declaration, and, where required by the treaty, substantiation that the shareholder has substantive economic activities. The withholding agent may apply the reduced treaty rate only after the application and documents are submitted and accepted, subject to the National Tax Service's post-filing verification.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding for cross-border royalties and interest is 22% (20% national tax plus 2% local surtax). Income tax treaty rates commonly reduce royalties to 15% and interest to 10% to 15%, depending on the residence treaty partner. Certain webtoon IP licensing fees with no valid business purpose may be recharacterized as dividends and lose treaty benefits.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: cross-border related-party transactions equal to or exceeding KRW 5 billion. Master File: annual revenue equal to or exceeding KRW 50 billion and cross-border related-party transactions equal to or exceeding KRW 5 billion. Country-by-Country Report: multinational group with consolidated revenue equal to or exceeding KRW 100 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea applies a substance-over-form principle and the general anti-abuse doctrine under the National Tax Basic Act. There is no statutory Economic Substance Regulations regime of the kind used in Gulf Cooperation Council jurisdictions, but the Korean tax authorities may disregard a corporate entity or transaction lacking genuine business purpose, employees, premises, and managerial functions. A webtoon IP holding company without economic substance in Korea will be refused treaty benefits and may be recharacterized as an artificial conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional omission of webtoon sales revenue derived from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, fabrication of expenses, use of grossly fraudulent invoices, or failure to file a corporate income tax return for consecutive years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of up to 40% of the underreported tax amount, daily overdue interest of approximately 0.022%, and criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act with imprisonment up to 3 years and a fine of up to twice the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Representative directors and actual controlling shareholders can be jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax under the National Tax Collection Act. Criminal conviction can result in imprisonment, travel restrictions, asset freezing, and restitution of the evaded amounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a Korean Chusik Hoesa with no office, no employees, no independent decision-making, and no operational function solely to hold foreign webtoon IP and pass dividends to a related offshore entity under a tax treaty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of treaty benefits, recharacterization of payments as taxable Korean-source dividends or royalties, assessment of corporate tax and withholding tax at the 22% statutory rate, and a 40% non-deduction penalty on unsupported related-party payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who cause the entity to operate as a mere shell may face secondary tax liability, personal liability for withheld dividend tax, travel bans pending tax collection, and potential criminal liability for intentional tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Shifting webtoon licensing profit to a low-tax foreign affiliate by paying excessive royalties from Korea, setting resale prices below arm's length, or using transactional manipulations with no commercial rationale.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income to the arm's length amount, disallowance of the excess royalty deduction, addition of 10% to 20% transfer pricing penalties on the adjusted amount, and interest accrual on the underpaid corporate tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and transfer pricing officers who knowingly execute inflated intercompany contracts may be held personally liable for the tax shortfall under the secondary liability rules, and may be prohibited from leaving the jurisdiction during the tax audit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving digital content proceeds into foreign accounts unreported to the Bank of Korea, failing to register inbound loan contracts, or laundering webtoon platform proceeds through opaque shell accounts or nominee shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines and imprisonment under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and Financial Information Analysis Act, including civil penalties up to KRW 200 million and criminal penalties of up to 5 years imprisonment for serious foreign exchange crimes. Unreported foreign income is also subject to tax reassessment and heavy penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can face personal restitution, court-ordered travel bans, confiscation of assets, and imprisonment where the foreign exchange violation was committed with intention or as a systematic corporate practice.
